findings.text: follow-on: the declared negative control does not discriminate. The mutation NOVA_TANGENT_COMPILE_HEAVY=1 doubles the tangent program, but its only demonstrated refusal (negative-control-graded-residual.log, EXIT=1) is on graded_residual, which already exceeds the 3.0 CPU bound without the mutation; the re-run on complete_pole and contract (negative-control.log) shows complete_pole still passing under the mutation at 2.20 and is cut mid-contract, so no passing row is shown turning red. The mutation lifts a passing row's CPU ratio by only about 12 percent (2.20 against a shipped 1.97), so it is too weak to cross the bound for any row that passes today. A stronger control (for example summing four copies, or mutating the smallest row) would show the guard firing on a state that would otherwise pass.

follow-on: the reviewed run's own delta arms are the source of the added-failure derivation, and both are incomplete. baseline_suite (delta-base.log) and after_suite and after (delta-after.log) are each completed:false with exit_status 124: five modules green and tests/biot/test_vertex_term_tangents.py cut by its own 300 s bound in both. More relevant to this node's change, the delta command selects -m 'not slow' and the assertion this node edits (test_tangent_compiles_within_three_primals) is slow-marked, so the delta arms never exercise the changed test; the four compile passes are its only evidence. The delta is still informative because the two arms are exactly symmetric and the cut module is unmodified, so no added failure is measured there, but the 'moves no module under tests/biot' claim rests on an arm set that excludes the changed row.

follow-on: the change moves one test id from pass to fail and the prescribed derivation cannot see it. At base the bound was asserted on wall, under which finite_part passed (wall ratio 2.30, from the pass1 log's 0.099/0.043) and graded_residual failed (wall 3.79); after, both fail on CPU (finite_part 4.59-4.67, graded_residual 4.47-3.48). So tests/biot now carries a red test_tangent_compiles_within_three_primals[finite_part] that was green at base. The node discloses this in the fragment (finite_part is the moved verdict) and it is the correct measure, but the delta arms exclude the slow rows, so this red id is unreachable from added_failure_ids derived from baseline_suite/after_suite. The coordinator should carry it as a known red on the CPU measure, not a delivered pass. The row's primal compile (0.044 s) is the smallest in the set, so the measure's own resolution is a large fraction of it, as the fragment notes.

follow-on: the asserted measure is time.process_time() inside the spawned probe, which counts CPU across all threads of the child; XLA compilation is multi-threaded, so the figure depends on how many threads the compile actually runs on that host. The four passes show the measure is stable under an eight-spinner load (every row moves at most 0.2 in ratio between a sequential and a loaded pass), so it is load-insensitive in the sense claimed; but a host with a different core count could shift the absolute CPU seconds. No action required for this node; recorded so a future rebaseline is not read as a regression.

gate_arms_note: The reviewed run recorded exactly the two arms I read (baseline_suite -> delta-base.log, after_suite -> delta-after.log); I did not need to reproduce a missing arm. Both are incomplete (EXIT=124, tests/biot/test_vertex_term_tangents.py cut by its own 300 s bound in base and after alike) and neither contains the changed compile-row assertion because both select -m 'not slow'. added_failure_count 0 and no added ids follow from the two logs as recorded.

justifications.durability: The guard is real: the three test modules assert ratio <= 3.0 (test_elliptic:470, test_range:363, test_vertex_edge:485); a compile row spawns 21 fresh processes, so the row gets its own @pytest.mark.timeout(1800) (test_elliptic:466, test_range:359, test_vertex_edge:481) while every other test keeps the repository default; and the mutation NOVA_TANGENT_COMPILE_HEAVY=1 is wired into the probe at :152-158 so it doubles only the tangent program. It is docked because the guard's discriminating power is not demonstrated by any log in the run. The declared control log (negative-control-graded-residual.log) refuses on graded_residual, which already exceeds the 3.0 bound without the mutation, so passing there is not evidence of discrimination; the fragment concedes this and re-ran on complete_pole and contract, but negative-control.log shows complete_pole still PASSING under the mutation at ratio 2.20 (its shipped ratio is about 1.97) before the log is cut mid-contract, so no passing row is ever shown turning red under the mutation.
justifications.evidence: The fragment's ten-row table reconciles exactly with the four pass logs: I read jobA-sequential-pass1.log, jobA-sequential-pass2.log, jobB-loaded-pass1.log and jobB-loaded-pass2.log and every ratio matches the table (complete_pole 1.97/1.98/2.15/2.14 ... finite_part 4.59/4.67/3.14/3.22, graded_residual 4.47/4.37/3.48/3.48), each pass reports '2 failed, 8 passed, 93 deselected', and the FAILED ids are exactly test_tangent_compiles_within_three_primals[finite_part] and [graded_residual] in all four passes. The wall-versus-CPU 'before' claim is verified exactly from pass1: graded_residual wall 0.531/0.140 = 3.79 and finite_part wall 0.099/0.043 = 2.30. Docked because the reviewed run's own delta arms (baseline_suite/after_suite) are both completed:false (EXIT=124, tests/biot/test_vertex_term_tangents.py cut by its own 300 s bound in both), and because the declared negative control's only demonstrated refusal is on a row already red.
justifications.fit: Every name is a mechanism name: _children_cpu_seconds, compile_row, compile_ratio, _median, median_cpu_seconds, median_process_cpu_seconds, compile_cpu_seconds. No plan, sprint, ticket or version identifier appears in any symbol, comment or docstring. The module docstring (:17-30) explains the physics of the measure -- descheduling under load, the import constant the whole-child CPU carries -- rather than citing a tracker entry.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal is to measure each fresh compile process by the CPU seconds it spends inside lowered.compile() (time.process_time() around exactly that call), assert the tangent-over-primal ratio on the median of seven CPU medians with the bound kept at 3.0, and print the wall and the whole-child CPU beside every arm. tests/biot/tangent_identity.py:171-175 takes the CPU around lowered.compile() inside the spawned probe, :237 asserts on median cpu, and :238-244 prints wall, cpu, process_cpu and equations; the bound is unchanged at 3.0 (test_elliptic:470, test_range:363, test_vertex_edge:485). The two rows that exceed it are named and left red rather than loosened, and the fragment states plainly that finite_part is the one row whose verdict the change moves. Docked one point because the discriminating half of the goal -- a control that shows the guard refuses a state that would otherwise pass -- is not demonstrated (see durability).
justifications.reuse: The change extends the existing compile_row/compile_ratio harness and its _COMPILE_PROBE rather than adding a second instrument: compile_row now also records the whole child's CPU from getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) deltas (:189, :207-209) and compile_ratio asserts on the same seven-median it already computed (:237). Docked for a small redundancy: _median (:214) sorts before np.median, which already sorts.
